title: The adulteress and her paramour brought the Saxon robbers here
html_source: The adulteress in question is “MacMurrough’s wife” Devorgilla (Derbforgaill or Derval), wife of Tiernan O'Rourke (Ua Ruaric), Prince of Breffni. Her fabled paramour was Dermot MacMurrough (Mac Murchada), King of Leinster. The story goes that while Prince O'Rourke was away, Devorgilla was “captured” (willingly, as is told) by King MacMurrough and taken back to his capital. Prince O'Rourke sought aid from Rory O'Connor, High King of Ireland, who had MacMurrough deposed. He sought refuge in Bristol and when denied help from Henry II of England, Henry’s enemy Richard de Clare (2nd Earl of Pembroke) was more receptive and with his forces regained his kingdom (in exchange for his daughter Aiofe MacMurrough’s hand in marriage). This opened the door for further conquest and subjugation of Ireland, which occurred later at the hands of Henry II in 1171, resulting in total Norman control of the island.
